name: Weer
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful village in the Unterinntal with the region’s largest outdoor swimming pool and stunning natural scenery.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The municipality of Weer is situated at an elevation of 558 metres above sea level in the Lower Inn Valley within the Schwaz district, approximately 20 kilometres east of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck. This charming nucleated village spreads across the wide, fertile alluvial fan of the Weerbach stream along the southern flank of the valley, with the torrent forming the boundary between the Schwaz and Innsbruck-Land districts. Home to roughly 1,800 residents, Weer is a sun-blessed, peaceful residential community characterised by longstanding agrarian roots, traditional orchards, and modern local enterprise. Sheltered beneath the foothills of the Tux Pre-Alps to the south and facing the limestone precipices of the Karwendel range across the Inn, Weer provides a tranquil retreat for relaxing holidays and outdoor exploration.

Geschichte

Human settlement on the alluvial fan reaches back to prehistoric times, attested by archaeological discoveries from the Bronze and Iron Ages. The community was first documented around 1075 in records of the Bishopric of Brixen under the entry 'in pago Weri', a name derived from Celtic roots signifying rushing water. During the Schwaz silver mining boom around 1500, the Weerbach stream gained regional renown for gold panning; this artisanal heritage is commemorated on the municipal coat of arms by a golden panning bowl over crossed mining hammers. The village's architectural masterpiece is the parish church of Saint Gallus: reconstructed between 1778 and 1779 by master builder Johann Michael Umhauser, it represents an outstanding Rococo sanctuary adorned with ceiling frescoes and illusionistic architecture by the celebrated Tyrolean painter Franz Anton Zeiller.

Anreise

Weer benefits from exceptional transport accessibility within the central Inn Valley corridor. Motorists access the village via the Inntal Autobahn A12 taking either the Wattens or Vomp/Schwaz exits, connecting directly along the federal highway B171 into town. Rail passengers travel along the Lower Inn Valley line to nearby stations at Pill-Vomperbach or Fritzens-Wattens, both served at half-hourly intervals by S-Bahn Tirol trains (lines S4 and S5) with swift connections to Innsbruck and Kufstein. Major express trains stop at the nearby transport hubs of Jenbach and Innsbruck Central Station. Furthermore, regional bus route 4111 connects Weer directly to neighbouring towns, while cyclists enjoy seamless access via the level Inn Cycle Path along the river.

Tipps

A cultural highlight is the parish church of St. Gallus, considered one of the finest Rococo sacred buildings in the Inn Valley, renowned for its luminous ceiling frescoes and stucco work. For hikers, the picturesque Weerbach Gorge offers refreshing, shaded forest paths winding along the rushing torrent up towards Kolsassberg and Weerberg. Cycling enthusiasts can join the Inn Cycle Path (Innradweg R1) along the riverbank for scenic, family-friendly rides toward the historic silver town of Schwaz or the medieval salt-trading town of Hall in Tirol. Peaceful walking trails meander through local orchard meadows, offering idyllic spots to pause and admire the dramatic limestone panoramas of the Karwendel range.
